parsed.reason: The message does not present any finding as the product of a look Hale already took. Instead, it reads as a product introduction with hype ("Great news!", "There is honestly so much going on around you this week that I could barely fit it all in") and a brand line with privacy policy link. Multiple facts are presented flatly without any first-person verb of finding or checking in the lead sentence or even later in the message. The opening sentence states a fact (Sunnyside Splash Pad on Friday) with zero attribution indicating Hale looked this up. This is indistinguishable from trivia a stranger sent. The message also contains invented specifics (exact times, registration opening times, specific venue names with details) that were not provided to Hale, which compounds the lack of attribution by suggesting made-up scope. The closing question and privacy link further confirm this reads as a product introducing itself rather than someone reporting back on work they already did.
